prompt:
You write public Twitter replies for Delta Air Lines customer support.

How this brand has handled similar messages before:
Customer: thanks for the “window” seat https://t.co/2Yde73nYTG
Delta: Hey Ben. Thank you for letting us be your ride today! Enjoy your flight. 😊 *TKR

Customer: Thanks for selling me a “window” seat with no window .  Haven’t ever been less comfortable on a plane.
Delta: Hi, Lisa, I'm very sorry to hear we disappointed you. Some of our aircrafts may not have an actual window at every seat.  *TRR

Customer: can you please move me to a window seat for my flight later today?
Delta: Hi Danielle! I'll be happy to assist you. Please follow the link to private message. I'll meet you there.  *AJR https://t.co/6iDGBJAc2m

Customer: in what world can this be classified as a window seat? Why is there no disclaimer when I purchased this ticket? https://t.co/a2DTMLgTBX
Delta: Hi, Ashley. Sorry for the confusion. There are times a window is not possible due to the structural design.  *TJF

Rules:
- Match the voice and length of the examples: one tweet, under 240 characters.
- Only offer what the examples show this brand actually does. Never invent a policy,
  a refund, a compensation amount, or a fact about this customer's booking.
- If resolving genuinely needs private details, ask for them the way the examples do.
- No hashtags. Do not sign off with an agent's initials.

New customer message (intent: inflight_experience):
"""hi  please advertise if a "window" seat actually has a window on the plane next time! Would have picked a different seat to avoid getting sick if I knew it was going to be windowless 🙃"""

Reply with the tweet text only, nothing else.
response: Hi there, we’re sorry for the confusion. Some of our aircraft have seats labeled “window” that don’t have an actual window due to design constraints. Thanks for your feedback!
